provenance: AI-assisted ensemble score authoring; explicit genre briefs, rhythmic cells and coordinated sentences. No runtime model.

blues.brief: Twelve-bar shuffle: a fifth/sixth (minor seventh in minor) riff, sparse walking links and short lead answers; drummer owns the last turnaround.

phrases.description: A repeated low riff answers once and leaves the last bar to the drummer.
The lead answer moves later in the next twelve-bar sentence.
Bass links are separated from the two guitar answers.
A reversed answering contour comes home without a competing bass fill.

rock.brief: Roots Rock: short low power-chord pulses open into ringing accents in the lift; bass pickups and open-guitar replies alternate.

phrases.description: Muted support opens briefly, with one guitar response.
Ringing accents shift within the second sentence.
One bass pickup and one open-guitar answer get separate windows.
The bass leads early and the guitar answers later.

country.brief: Country two-step: short boom-chick strokes, root/fifth upright and clean electric double-stop answers, never a constant lead solo.

phrases.description: The two-step stays uncluttered, with a small closing brush turn.
One understated upstroke varies the second sentence.
Electric double stops answer before a separate upright pickup.
A falling electric answer leads back to the boom-chick.

strummed.brief: Strummed Folk: broad bass-and-brush gestures, selective upstrokes and ringing cadences, without Country twang or a clipped two-step.

phrases.description: Long brushes and a ringing close keep the accompaniment open.
A second broad sentence shifts the sustained accents.
Light upstrokes appear selectively and relax at the cadence.
Sustained and brushed bars alternate without dense fills.

reggae.brief: Reggae: a repeating two-bar bass hook, dry offbeat skanks and a restrained organ bubble; replies create space rather than adding a rock fill.

phrases.description: The two-bar bass idea repeats under a light bubble.
Bubble and skank gaps vary while the hook remains recognizable.
The guitar and organ leave room for a single bass answer.
The organ answers in the window used by bass in the prior sentence.

funk.brief: Pocket Funk: a stable syncopated bass cell, clipped guitar accents and quiet scratches; bass and guitar answers do not compete.

phrases.description: Repeating syncopation and quiet scratch strokes leave space.
A few omitted guitar accents vary the answer without filling every gap.
A ghosted bass answer and clipped guitar reply have separate bars.
The next sentence reverses which instrument answers first.

soul.brief: Mellow Soul: warm rootless sixth/minor-seventh keyboard calls, quiet melodic guitar responses, laid-back bass and deliberate breathing space. Reviewed for open spacing: major 6/9 colour in fourths, open suspensions, and a consonant third-root-fifth close.

phrases.description: A warm call and a late guitar reply leave the rest of the phrase open.
The suspended colour and guitar response move later.
Keyboard answers, guitar response and bass pickup are deliberately separated.
A falling guitar response leads back to a simple sustained cadence.
